name: Start-bright-then-filter pad: pick a harmonically rich (buzzy/bright) oscillator, odd unison 5-9, slow wavetable-position sweep, then low-pass to smooth it (keeping top-end headroom to automate back in), big low-cut reverb, low-cut EQ and a stereo imager to pull the pad around the listener; plus an attack-removed swell pad from any played source
goal: Make smooth, lush ambient pads that can still get bright on demand: start from a source with lots of high harmonics and remove highs with a synth filter (not an end-of-chain EQ), so the cutoff can be automated to bring brightness and air back for tension. Delta vs the brightness cluster: the 'rich source -> filter -> space' order, odd vs even unison as solid vs unstable, imager after big reverb to bring a distant pad back around the ears, and volume-swelling any played source (guitar, piano, vocal) so the reverb is fed only by the tone, not the attack.

source.title: Sound Design - Ambient Pads and Atmospheres

prerequisites: Any synth with wavetable or saw oscillators, unison, a 12/18/24 dB low-pass and an LFO or envelope as mod source
Reverb with low-cut, EQ, stereo imager/width control
Optional: a recorded or sampled played source (guitar, piano, vocal) and a gain/volume envelope

inputs.name: chords
inputs.description: Chords, a counter-line or a single held note for the pad

outputs.name: smooth_pad
outputs.description: Smooth, wide pad whose brightness is controlled by one filter-cutoff lane

outputs.name: swell_pad
outputs.description: Optional attack-free swell pad from a played source

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Steady pitch: the source adds a slow fine-tune LFO for analog drift; leave it out (Matt prefers steady pitch). Use wavetable-position motion instead.
Brightness comes from the source and the filter cutoff, not from a late treble boost.
Cut pad low end (and low reverb) if another bass element is in the mix.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Set amp attack and release to about 400-500 ms each as a starting point, then tailor to the part.
steps.expect: Notes fade in and out softly

steps.action: Choose a bright, buzzy, harmonically rich oscillator (a saw, or a PWM/analog-style wavetable). Try many; keep the one with the most high-end energy and character.
steps.expect: Raw tone sounds bright, even harsh

steps.action: Unison: an odd voice count (5, 7 or 9) gives a solid centre voice with voices spread either side; below 5 is not lush, above 9 costs CPU. For a rougher 'organic' pad, use an even count (e.g. 4): no centre voice gives a slightly unstable, edgy quality. Detune stays static.
steps.expect: Lush wide tone (odd) or deliberately unstable tone (even)

steps.action: Optional motion: route a slow LFO or long envelope to wavetable position so it sweeps gently through the table.
steps.expect: Timbre morphs slowly; pitch stays fixed

steps.action: Low-pass the tone inside the synth (12 or 18 dB/oct; 18 gives a more pronounced cutoff) until smooth, then raise volume to compensate. Use the filter rather than an EQ so the cutoff can be automated to reintroduce highs for builds.
steps.expect: Smooth pad with brightness available on one automation lane

steps.action: Space: a very large reverb at high mix with plenty of low-cut (filter before or after reverb, either order works), then an EQ cutting excess low end and optionally a second reverb.
Add a stereo imager after the reverbs and A/B: without it the pad sits far in front; with it the pad wraps around the listener.

Swell variant: play chords or a melody on any source (guitar, piano, vocal), start slightly before the bar, and put a gain envelope first in the chain that rises from 0 at the bar so the attack is removed. Then low-cut EQ, imager, and reverb, which is now fed only by the swell.
steps.expect: Attack-free tone swells into reverb and decays into the next chord

verification: Filter-cutoff automation alone audibly moves the pad from smooth to bright (high harmonics exist in the source).
Odd-unison version sounds solid; even-unison version audibly rougher.
With imager on, the side level rises and the mono fold-down still keeps the pad.
Swell variant: no audible pluck transient before the reverb bloom.
No pitch modulation in the patch.
